$comment: Manual layout nudges, applied LAST by src/layout.ts — after projection, radial compression
and overlap relaxation. Keys are `Station Name|operator-id`, because a name alone is
ambiguous (Ghatkopar, Marol Naka and Chembur each exist on two operators).
Coordinates are in canvas units: 1000 x 1500, origin top-left, y increasing downward.
This file is intentionally EMPTY for now. The automated pipeline places all 218 stations and
the collision-avoiding label placer positions 88 of 92 candidate labels, which is legible
enough to review and ship behind the app's zoom-based level-of-detail. Hand-tuning positions
is a visual task that needs a human iterating on out/layout.svg, and guessing coordinates
without looking would make the map worse, not better.
KNOWN CROWDED AREAS, in priority order — these are where nudges will earn their keep:
1. The Andheri cluster. Six stations across four operators sit within ~120 units:
Andheri (suburban, Western + Harbour), Andheri (Metro Line 1), Andheri (West) and
D. N. Nagar (Metro 2A), Versova (Metro 1), Gundavali and Western Express Highway
(eastbound) (Metro 1/7). Their labels overlap and four labels are currently dropped.
2. South Mumbai below Dadar, where Line 3 runs parallel to the Western and Harbour lines
through a narrow strip.
3. Dadar itself — Western, Central and Line 3 stations plus the Monorail nearby.
How to work on it: run `npm run layout`, open out/layout.svg in a browser, drag-read the
coordinates you want from the rendered positions, add entries here, and re-run. Each entry
must carry a `reason` so a later maintainer can tell a deliberate nudge from a stray edit.
